claim: Resolving patterns of synaptic connectivity in neural circuits currently requires serial section electron microscopy.
source: Resolving patterns of synaptic connectivity in neural circuits currently requires serial section electron microscopy.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract presenting the current state of the field.

claim: Complete circuit reconstruction is prohibitively slow.
source: However, complete circuit reconstruction is prohibitively slow and may not be necessary for many purposes such as comparing neuronal structure and connectivity among multiple animals.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current methods.

claim: Viral vectors can deliver peroxidase derivatives to genetically identify neurons.
source: We used viral vectors to deliver peroxidase derivatives, which catalyze production of an electron-dense tracer, to genetically identify neurons
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Peroxidase derivatives catalyze production of an electron-dense tracer.
source: We used viral vectors to deliver peroxidase derivatives, which catalyze production of an electron-dense tracer, to genetically identify neurons
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the peroxidase derivatives.

claim: A protocol was developed that enhances the electron-density of labeled cells while retaining ultrastructure quality.
source: and developed a protocol that enhances the electron-density of the labeled cells while retaining the quality of the ultrastructure.
evidence: This describes a methodological development in the study.

claim: High contrast of marked neurons enables targeted high-resolution reimaging of regions selected from rapidly-acquired lower resolution reconstruction.
source: The high contrast of the marked neurons enabled two innovations that speed data acquisition: targeted high-resolution reimaging of regions selected from rapidly-acquired lower resolution reconstruction
evidence: This describes one of the innovations enabled by the method.

claim: High contrast of marked neurons enables an unsupervised segmentation algorithm.
source: The high contrast of the marked neurons enabled two innovations that speed data acquisition: targeted high-resolution reimaging of regions selected from rapidly-acquired lower resolution reconstruction, and an unsupervised segmentation algorithm.
evidence: This describes the second innovation enabled by the method.

claim: The pipeline reduces imaging and reconstruction times by two orders of magnitude.
source: This pipeline reduces imaging and reconstruction times by two orders of magnitude, facilitating directed inquiry of circuit motifs.
evidence: This is a quantitative claim about the improvement in efficiency.

claim: Only electron microscopy provides sufficient resolution to visualize the complete complement of synapses that neurons form and receive.
source: At present, however, only electron microscopy (EM) provides sufficient resolution to visualize the complete complement of synapses that neurons form and receive.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of electron microscopy compared to other methods.

claim: Large-scale reconstructions from serial sections have provided deep insights into neuronal circuit principles.
source: Indeed, large-scale reconstructions from serial sections have provided deep insights into neuronal circuit principles (Briggman et al., 2011; Bock et al., 2011; Takemura et al., 2013; Morgan et al., 2016) .
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Saturated reconstruction of volumes around 1000 μm3 is feasible.
source: Advances in sectioning, imaging and segmentation methods make so-called 'saturated' reconstruction of volumes around 1000 μm3 feasible (Kasthuri et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Saturated reconstruction remains challenging when multiple samples must be compared.
source: Even these modest volumes remain challenging, however, and when multiple samples must be compared -e.g., controls vs. mutant or treated vs. untreated animals - this approach is currently out of reach (Plaza et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Neuronal activity can be monitored using calcium indicators, then neurons with particular patterns of activity can be relocated in thin sections and reconstructed.
source: For example, neuronal activity can be monitored using calcium indicators, then neurons with particular patterns of activity can be relocated in thin sections and reconstructed (Briggman et al., 2011; Bock et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes an alternative approach supported by citations.

claim: Calcium indicator-based reconstruction is technically demanding and infeasible in many tissues.
source: This method is, however, technically demanding and infeasible in many tissues.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the calcium indicator method.

claim: Horseradish peroxidase (HRP) catalyzes the formation of a 3,3'-diaminobenzidine (DAB) polymer.
source: A classical ultrastructural tracer is horseradish peroxidase (HRP), which catalyzes the formation of a 3,3'-diaminobenzidine (DAB) polymer
evidence: This describes the mechanism of HRP as a tracer.

claim: The DAB polymer binds osmium and is thereby rendered electron-dense.
source: the polymer binds osmium and is thereby rendered electron-dense.
evidence: This describes how the DAB polymer becomes visible in EM.

claim: Recombinant HRP is enzymatically inactive in the cytosol because it fails to form disulfide bonds or become glycosylated.
source: Recombinant HRP is enzymatically inactive in the cytosol because it fails to form disulfide bonds or become glycosylated
evidence: This explains why recombinant HRP doesn't work in the cytosol.

claim: HRP inactivity in the cytosol can be overcome by directing the protein to topologically extracellular compartments such as vesicles.
source: but this limitation can be overcome by directing the protein to topologically extracellular compartments such as vesicles (Li et al., 2010; Atasoy et al., 2014; Schikorski et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes a solution to the HRP inactivity problem, supported by citations.

claim: An HRP variant was generated that was codon-optimized, mutated to increase activity, and fused to an endoplasmic reticulum targeting sequence (erHRP).
source: We therefore generated an HRP variant that was codon-optimized, mutated to increase activity, and fused to an endoplasmic reticulum targeting sequence (erHRP).
evidence: This describes the construction of the erHRP variant.

claim: APX and APEX2 are derivatives of plant ascorbate peroxidases that are active in the cytosol.
source: We also tested derivatives of plant ascorbate peroxidases called APX and APEX2, which are active in the cytosol (Martell et al., 2012; Lam et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the properties of APX and APEX2, supported by citations.

claim: All three peroxidase constructs (erHRP, APX, APEX2) generated active peroxidase in transfected HEK293 cells.
source: Initial studies using cultured HEK293 cells confirmed that all three constructs generated active peroxidase in the transfected cells (Figure 1a,b and data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1a,b.

claim: APEX2NES renders HEK-cells photon-dense by DAB polymerization.
source: (a–b) Bright-field images of HEK-cells rendered photon-dense by DAB polymerization, catalyzed either by APEX2 tagged with a nuclear export signal (APEX2NES) (a) or endoplasmic reticulum tagged HRP (erHRP) (b).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1a.

claim: erHRP renders HEK-cells photon-dense by DAB polymerization.
source: (a–b) Bright-field images of HEK-cells rendered photon-dense by DAB polymerization, catalyzed either by APEX2 tagged with a nuclear export signal (APEX2NES) (a) or endoplasmic reticulum tagged HRP (erHRP) (b).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1b.

claim: APEX2NES renders direction-selective retinal ganglion cells (ooDSGC) photon-dense.
source: (c–d) Bright-field images of direction-selective retinal ganglion cells (ooDSGC) expressing APEX2NES (c) or erHRP (d) and rendered photon-dense as in (a).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1c.

claim: erHRP renders direction-selective retinal ganglion cells (ooDSGC) photon-dense.
source: (c–d) Bright-field images of direction-selective retinal ganglion cells (ooDSGC) expressing APEX2NES (c) or erHRP (d) and rendered photon-dense as in (a).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Standard EM staining protocol showed no detectable cytosolic DAB-polymer staining in HEK-cells.
source: (f–g) EM-micrographs of HEK-cells rendered electron-dense after DAB-polymerization as in (a). A standard EM staining protocol showed no detectable cytosolic DAB-polymer staining (f)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Addition of a reduction step dramatically enhanced DAB-polymer staining in HEK-cells.
source: whereas the addition of a reduction step dramatically enhanced DAB-polymer staining (g).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Ultrastructure is well preserved after reduction in ribbon synapses in the outer plexiform layer.
source: (h) Ribbon synapses in the outer plexiform layer; ultrastructure is well preserved after reduction.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1h.

claim: An ooDSGC soma expressing APEX2 is rendered electron dense after tissue reduction.
source: (i) EM-micrograph of an ooDSGC soma (arrowhead) rendered electron dense after tissue reduction next to a non-expressing RGC (asterisk).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1i.

claim: Cytosolic APEX2 staining is visible in EM.
source: (j) Close-up of cytosolic APEX2 staining.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1j.

claim: Dendritic processes expressing APEX2 are contacted by presynaptic partners in the inner plexiform layer.
source: (k) Dendritic processes expressing APEX2 (asterisk) contacted by a presynaptic partner (arrowhead) in the inner plexiform layer.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1k.

claim: Axonal long-range projections of APEX2-expressing ooDSGCs are visible in the superior colliculus.
source: (l) Axonal long-range projections of an APEX2-expressing ooDSGC in the superior colliculus (asterisk) with a postsynaptic target (arrowhead).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1l.

claim: erHRP-expressing RGCs are visible next to non-expressing RGCs in EM.
source: (m) erHRP-expressing (arrowhead) RGC next to a non-expressing RGC (asterisk).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1m.

claim: erHRP staining is visible in J-RGC soma and dendrites.
source: (n,o) Close-up of erHRP staining of a J-RGC soma (n) and dendrite (o) (arrowhead point to presynaptic partners).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1n,o.

claim: Long DAB reaction times (5 hr) allowed visualizing the DAB-polymer using a standard EM-staining protocol, but severely deteriorated the quality of the ultrastructure.
source: (a) EM-micrograph of an APEX2NES expressing process. Long DAB reaction times (5 hr) allowed visualizing the DAB-polymer using a standard EM-staining protocol, but severely deteriorated the quality of the ultrastructure.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Under conditions optimized to preserve good ultrastructure, DAB-polymer signals were absent or very weak.
source: (b) EM-micrograph of an RGC using a fixation and staining protocol optimized to preserve good ultrastructure. Under these conditions, DAB-polymer signals were absent or very weak, as exemplified by the weakly stained soma (encircled with asterisk) and its corresponding unstained process (encircled).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Using the standard protocol, no or very weak signal was detected using the osmium staining in APEX2NES expressing HEK-cells.
source: Using the standard protocol, no or very weak signal was detected using the osmium (c) or the rOTO (e) staining, respectively.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Using the standard protocol, very weak signal was detected using the rOTO staining in APEX2NES expressing HEK-cells.
source: Using the standard protocol, no or very weak signal was detected using the osmium (c) or the rOTO (e) staining, respectively. Asterisks in (e) depict weakly stained HEK-cell.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Reducing the tissue dramatically enhanced the signal in both osmium and rOTO staining conditions in APEX2NES expressing HEK-cells.
source: In contrast, reducing the tissue dramatically enhanced the signal in both conditions (d–f).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d,f.

claim: The heme content in erythrocytes catalyzes the DAB reaction producing a strong precipitate.
source: (g–h) Bright-field images of erythrocytes in retinal tissue after DAB-polymerization (arrowheads) before (g) and after the reduction step (h). The heme content in erythrocytes catalyzes the DAB reaction producing a strong precipitate that is enhanced by a reduction step.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1g,h.

claim: The reduction enhances the DAB-polymer's affinity to osmium in erythrocytes.
source: (i–j) EM-micrograph of erythrocytes using the rOTO staining protocol in standard (i) and reduced (j) conditions. The reduction enhances the DAB-polymer's affinity to osmium.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1i,j.

claim: A mouse direction selective RGC soma is rendered electron dense after tissue reduction.
source: EM-micrograph of a mouse direction selective RGC soma rendered electron dense after tissue reduction (arrowhead). Note the small process visible in the inner plexiform layer (boxes, enlarged image on the right) and the strongest signal of the erythrocytes (asterisk).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cre-dependent virally infected mouse direction-selective retinal ganglion cells expressing erHRP are rendered photon-dense.
source: (a) Bright-field images of Cre-dependent virally infected mouse direction-selective retinal ganglion cell (ooDSGC) expressing erHRP and rendered photon-dense.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a.

claim: An erHRP expressing RGC is visible in a vertical retinal cross-section.
source: (b) EM-micrograph of a vertical retinal cross-section with an erHRP expressing RGC. Asterisk depicts erHRP-expressing soma.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b.

claim: erHRP expressing soma is visible in EM.
source: (c) erHRP expressing soma.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3c.

claim: erHRP expressing dendritic compartments are visible in the IPL.
source: (d–e) erHRP expressing dendritic compartments in the IPL.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3d,e.

claim: Ultra-structural quality is preserved in ribbon synapses in the IPL after erHRP expression and reduction.
source: (f) Micrograph of ribbon synapses in the IPL (arrowheads). Ultra-structural quality is preserved.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3f.

claim: The reduction step enhances the membrane and synaptic density stain compared to standard protocol.
source: (a–b). EM-micrographs of the inner plexiform layer of mouse retinas not treated with DAB and stained with the standard (a) or reduction protocol (b). Note the enhancement of the membrane and synaptic density stain in (b) compared to (a).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4a,b.

claim: The reduction shifts the distribution of the membrane pixels by 24 intensity values to a lower mean value compared to the cytosolic distribution.
source: (c–d) Intensity histograms of manually selected membrane or cytosol pixels from standard and reduced EM micrographs. The reduction shifts the distribution of the membrane pixels (black traces) by 24 intensity values to a lower mean value (μ) compared to the cytosolic distribution (gray traces; Intensity values: 0 = dark; 255 = white).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4c,d.

claim: The reduction step increases the electron density of membranes specifically.
source: Thus, the reduction step increases the electron density of membranes specifically.
evidence: This is inferred from the intensity histogram data.

claim: Contrast-to-noise improves by 62% by reducing the tissue.
source: Contrast-to-noise improves by 62% by reducing the tissue and therefore could be a valuable signal enhancing step to improve automatic segmentation results that are based on machine-learning approaches.
evidence: This is calculated from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4c,d.

claim: Reduced tissue was selected ~3 times more frequently than unreduced tissue in blind-to-condition selection of synaptic quality.
source: When we asked blind-to-condition observers to judge the quality of synapses between both conditions, the reduced tissue was selected ~3 times more frequently than unreduced tissue (Figure 1—figure supplement 4e).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4e.

claim: APEX2 in ooDS ganglion cells is contacted by presynaptic partners in the inner plexiform layer.
source: (a) EM-micrographs of the inner plexiform layer of mouse retinas expressing APEX2 in ooDS ganglion cells contacted by presynaptic partners (arrowheads).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5a.

claim: Axonal termini of APEX2 in ooDS ganglion cells contact postsynaptic partners in the superior colliculus.
source: (b) EM-micrographs of the upper layers of the superior colliculus including axonal termini of APEX2 in ooDS ganglion cells contacting postsynaptic partners (arrowheads).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: erHRP expressing ganglion cells are contacted by presynaptic partners in the inner plexiform layer.
source: (c) EM-micrographs of the inner plexiform layer of retinas expressing erHRP in ganglion cells (asterisks) contacted by presynaptic partners (arrowheads).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5c.

claim: Radicals produced during the long peroxidase reaction might oxidize the relevant functional groups in the polymer, leaving it photon-absorbent but inert to osmium.
source: We reasoned that radicals produced during the long peroxidase reaction might oxidize the relevant functional groups in the polymer, leaving it photon-absorbent but inert to osmium.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Reduction of functional groups on the polymer could restore reactivity to osmium.
source: If this were true, reduction of functional groups on the polymer could restore reactivity to osmium (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested by the authors, illustrated in Figure 1e.

claim: When HEK cells were treated with 5 mM sodium hydrosulfite between the peroxidase reaction and osmication, they were highly electron-dense.
source: However, when the HEK cells were treated with a mild reducing agent (5 mM sodium hydrosulfite) between the peroxidase reaction and osmication, they were highly electron-dense (Figure 1f,g).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1f,g.

claim: The rOTO protocol showed a slight improvement over conventional osmium staining, probably due to the change in the redox state of osmium tetroxide.
source: This was the case using either conventional osmium staining or an enhanced 'double osmium' staining protocol (rOTO), although the latter showed a slight improvement probably due to the change in the redox state of osmium tetroxide (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c–f; see Methods).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c–f.

claim: APX labeled the cytoplasm diffusely.
source: As expected, APX and APEX2NES labeled the cytoplasm diffusely (Figure 1j)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1j.

claim: APEX2NES labeled the cytoplasm diffusely.
source: As expected, APX and APEX2NES labeled the cytoplasm diffusely (Figure 1j)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1j.

claim: erHRP labeled membrane-bound intracellular compartments.
source: while erHRP labeled membrane-bound intracellular compartments (Figure 1n).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1n.

claim: APX and erHRP could be used as orthogonal labels.
source: Thus they could be used as orthogonal labels, although we have not yet pursued this application.
evidence: This is inferred from the different labeling patterns.

claim: The strength of the signal allowed identification of small stained dendritic profiles.
source: The strength of the signal allowed us to identify small stained dendritic profiles (Figure 1k,o)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1k,o.

claim: The strength of the signal allowed viewing the terminals of RGCs in the superior colliculus, approximately 1 cm from the somata.
source: and to view the terminals of RGCs in the superior colliculus, approximately 1 cm from the somata (Figure 1l).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1l.

claim: The reduction protocol actually improved the visualization of the ultrastructure irrespective of peroxidase expression or DAB treatment.
source: Remarkably, the reduction protocol actually improved the visualization of the ultrastructure irrespective of peroxidase expression or DAB treatment (Figure 1h).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1h.

claim: Part of the improvement resulted from an increase in the reactivity of membranes to osmium, thereby enhancing membrane-cytoplasm contrast.
source: Part of the improvement resulted from an increase in the reactivity of membranes to osmium, thereby enhancing membrane-cytoplasm contrast (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The improvement is also visible in the staining strength of synaptic densities.
source: This improvement is also visible in the staining strength of synaptic densities (Figure 1—figure supplement 4a,b).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4a,b.

claim: Peroxidase expression does not affect synapse formation.
source: When analyzing our datasets, we could not detect any structural differences between tissues expressing either of the peroxidases.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the datasets.

claim: The number of synapses counted in peroxidase expressing and control sections was similar, 0.32 and 0.34 synapses / μm2, respectively.
source: The number of synapses counted in peroxidase expressing and control sections was also similar, 0.32 and 0.34 synapses / μm2, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of synapse density.

claim: Cells presynaptic to APEX2 or erHRP could be clearly identified based on ultrastructural details.
source: Cells presynaptic to APEX2 or erHRP could be clearly identified based on ultrastructural details (Figure 1—figure supplement 5a,c).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5a,c.

claim: Postsynaptic partners of APEX2-expressing cells could be identified.
source: Postsynaptic partners of APEX2-expressing cells could also be identified.
evidence: This is stated based on the data.

claim: Synaptic vesicles of APEX2-expressing neurons could be detected in presynaptic terminals because they were unstained, and thereby contrasted with the electron-dense cytosol.
source: Moreover, synaptic vesicles of APEX2-expressing neurons could be detected in presynaptic terminals because they were unstained, and thereby contrasted with the electron-dense cytosol.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: The endoplasmic reticulum did not regularly extend to axonal terminals, making it difficult to identify postsynaptic partners of erHRP expressing ganglion cells.
source: However, the endoplasmic reticulum did not regularly extend to axonal terminals, making it difficult to identify postsynaptic partners of erHRP expressing ganglion cells.
evidence: This is an observation about the limitation of erHRP.

claim: APEX fused to GFP was expressed in direction-selective tangential cells of Drosophila melanogaster.
source: To test the generality of the method we expressed APEX fused to GFP in direction-selective tangential cells of Drosophila melanogaster (Joesch et al., 2008) (DB331-Gal4 → UAS-APEX-GFP; see Methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental setup in Drosophila.

claim: The DB331-Gal4 driver line expresses mainly in 6 vertically sensitive and 3 horizontally sensitive tangential cells.
source: This driver line expresses mainly in 6 vertically sensitive and 3 horizontally sensitive tangential cells.
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of the driver line.

claim: The expression pattern in Drosophila was apparent using either GFP fluorescence or the polymerized DAB to mark the cells.
source: This expression pattern was apparent using either GFP fluorescence or the polymerized DAB to mark the cells (Figure 2a,b).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2a,b.

claim: The electron dense precipitate of APEX expressing processes is visible in the fly's optic lobes.
source: We were also able to visualize the electron dense precipitate of these processes in the fly's optic lobes (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: Ultrastructural detail was reasonable in Drosophila tissue.
source: Although our method was optimized for mammalian tissue, ultrastructural detail was reasonable (Figure 2e)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Synaptic contacts made by and onto APEX expressing cells could be identified in Drosophila.
source: and allowed the identification of synaptic contacts made by and onto APEX expressing cells (Figure 2f–h).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2f–h.

claim: Peroxidase-stained neurites can be identified at overview resolution (20–30 nm per pixel).
source: Because we could identify small peroxidase-stained neurites at overview resolution (20–30 nm per pixel), we tested the minimal requirements to reconstruct both cell types at these resolutions.
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: Rapidly imaging every 10th section (270 nm separation), at 30 nm resolution was sufficient for mapping a J-RGC dendrite.
source: Rapidly imaging every 10th section (270 nm separation), at 30 nm resolution was sufficient for mapping a J-RGC dendrite (144 sections covering > 1 × 107 µm3, imaged in 22 hr; Figure 3a,b).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3a,b.

claim: Imaging the same volume at high resolution (4 nm/pixel) would have taken ~2500 hr on the same microscope.
source: By comparison, imaging the same volume at high resolution (4 nm/pixel) would have taken ~2500 hr on the same microscope.
evidence: This is a calculation based on imaging times.

claim: Manual reconstruction of the J-RGC took 2 worker-hours.
source: Manual reconstruction of the J-RGC was straightforward and took 2 worker-hours (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3c.

claim: All 1260 sections from a bloc with APEX2NES-positive SACs were imaged and SAC processes were reconstructed in this volume.
source: To extend this result to another cell type, we imaged all 1260 sections from a bloc with APEX2NES-positive SACs and reconstructed SAC processes in this volume (Figure 3d–f).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3d–f.

claim: 20 nm resolution is sufficient for viewing neurites.
source: Although 20 nm resolution is sufficient for viewing neurites, it does not allow optimal visualization of synaptic contacts (Figure 3g–h).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3g–h.

claim: 20 nm resolution does not allow optimal visualization of synaptic contacts.
source: Although 20 nm resolution is sufficient for viewing neurites, it does not allow optimal visualization of synaptic contacts (Figure 3g–h).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3g–h.

claim: Sections generated using ATUM are collected on wafers, and can be re-imaged.
source: However, sections generated using ATUM are collected on wafers, and can be re-imaged
evidence: This describes a feature of the ATUM method.

claim: Wafer-Mapper facilitates returning to the same place on a given section with micron-level precision.
source: a program, Wafer-Mapper (Hayworth et al., 2014), facilitates returning to the same place on a given section with micron-level precision.
evidence: This describes the function of Wafer-Mapper, supported by a citation.

claim: Targeted imaging at high resolution of areas chosen from the rapidly acquired, lower resolution reconstruction substantially reduces imaging time.
source: This feature allows targeted imaging at high resolution of areas chosen from the rapidly acquired, lower resolution reconstruction, thereby substantially reducing imaging time.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the benefit of the multi-scale approach.

claim: A heavily-labeled ~5 × 105 µm3 volume was selected from the overview-resolution reconstruction of ~2 × 107 µm3 and acquired at high-resolution (4 nm/pixel) in 250 hr.
source: We selected a heavily-labeled ~5 × 105 µm3 volume from the overview-resolution reconstruction of ~2 × 107 µm3 and acquired a high-resolution (4 nm/pixel) data set in 250 hr (Figure 3i).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3i.

claim: The multi-scale approach amounts to a 40-fold reduction in imaging time compared to a completely high-resolution approach.
source: Compared to a completely high-resolution approach, this amounts to a 40-fold reduction in imaging time.
evidence: This is a calculation based on imaging times.

claim: The multi-scale approach expedited reconstruction by constraining efforts to defined regions of interest.
source: More importantly, it expedited reconstruction, the current time-limiting step in connectomics (Plaza et al., 2014), by constraining efforts to defined regions of interest.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the benefit of the approach, supported by a citation.

claim: Multiple SAC-SAC interactions were observed in the SAC plexus.
source: We manually traced and reconstructed the SAC plexus in this volume, observing multiple SAC-SAC interactions, dendritic fasciculation in the SAC plexus and dendritic branching (Figure 3j,k and data not shown).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3j,k.

claim: Dendritic fasciculation was observed in the SAC plexus.
source: We manually traced and reconstructed the SAC plexus in this volume, observing multiple SAC-SAC interactions, dendritic fasciculation in the SAC plexus and dendritic branching (Figure 3j,k and data not shown).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3j,k.

claim: Dendritic branching was observed in the SAC plexus.
source: We manually traced and reconstructed the SAC plexus in this volume, observing multiple SAC-SAC interactions, dendritic fasciculation in the SAC plexus and dendritic branching (Figure 3j,k and data not shown).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3j,k.

claim: An algorithm was developed that detects and segments APEX2-positive processes, taking advantage of the high contrast rendered by the DAB polymer.
source: Finally, to further expedite the reconstruction pipeline, we developed an algorithm that detects and segments APEX2-positive processes, taking advantage of the high contrast rendered by the DAB polymer.
evidence: This describes the development of the segmentation algorithm.

claim: The algorithm is fast, parameterized and does not rely on the supervised machine learning training regimes currently required for lower contrast material.
source: Our algorithm is fast, parameterized and does not rely on the supervised machine learning training regimes currently required for lower contrast material (Kasthuri et al., 2015) (Figure 4a, Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the properties of the algorithm, with a citation for comparison.

claim: A recall statistic of 91.8% was calculated for the 2D segmentation portion of the algorithm.
source: We calculated a recall statistic of 91.8% for the 2D segmentation portion of the algorithm (Figure 4b,c).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4b,c.

claim: All missed segments were small (on average 45 × 42 pixels), and were seldom necessary to establish connectivity.
source: All missed segments were small (on average 45 × 42 pixels), and were seldom necessary to establish connectivity.
evidence: This is an analysis of the algorithm's performance.

claim: The algorithm could reconstruct the main characteristics of the dendritic processes and recapitulated most of the manually segmented details.
source: Our algorithm could reconstruct the main characteristics of the dendritic processes and recapitulated most of the manually segmented details (Figure 4d,e).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4d,e.

claim: The algorithm is two orders of magnitude faster than approaches based on convolutional neural networks for membrane classification.
source: The primary advantage of this approach is processing time, being two orders of magnitude faster than approaches based on convolutional neural networks for membrane classification (Kasthuri et al., 2015; Kaynig et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison of processing times, supported by citations.

claim: Training regimes in the neural network approaches require adjusting at least thousands of parameters separately for each new tissue.
source: Training regimes in the neural network approaches require adjusting at least thousands of parameters separately for each new tissue
evidence: This describes a limitation of neural network approaches.

claim: The algorithm incorporates unsupervised components with a small fixed set of tunable parameters.
source: in contrast, our algorithm incorporates unsupervised components with a small fixed set of tunable parameters (see Methods and Supplementary Code).
evidence: This describes an advantage of the algorithm.

claim: The high contrast-to-noise ratio of the peroxidase-labeled cells is the enabling factor for the efficacy of the algorithm.
source: Importantly, the high contrast-to-noise ratio of the peroxidase-labeled cells is the enabling factor for the efficacy of this algorithm
evidence: This is a conclusion about what makes the algorithm work.

claim: The algorithm could be used for reconstruction of DAB-stained structures in any tissue.
source: which means that it could be used for reconstruction of DAB-stained structures in any tissue.
evidence: This is an inference about the generalizability of the algorithm.

claim: Detailed synaptic properties may be obscured by the electron-dense stain.
source: Thus, although detailed synaptic properties may be obscured by the electron-dense stain, our methods are well-suited for rapid reconstruction of targeted neuron morphology and connectivity.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

evidence: This describes a step in the automatic segmentation algorithm, with a citation.

evidence: This describes a step in the automatic segmentation algorithm.

evidence: This describes a step in the automatic segmentation algorithm.

evidence: This describes a step in the automatic segmentation algorithm, with a citation.
